policy: Every active Renderer used by the benchmark must inherit one and only one registered scene-domain metadata scope. The scope must state manufacture/installation logic and link to detailed machine-readable contracts. A renderer parented outside these scopes is a metadata critical defect; source coverage never substitutes for rendered evidence.

domains.manufacture: Landscape/plaza fallback assembled from compacted ground support, paved or soil/grass finish zones, kerb/drain interfaces and metre-scaled surface layers; decorative shading is not baked into geometry or albedo.
domains.dimensionsThickness: Generated visible base layers are approximately 30-160 mm thick depending on grass, paving and worn-path support; kerb/drain/joint dimensions remain explicit in the ground infrastructure contracts.
domains.materialsFinish: Dry summer grass/soil, non-metallic concrete/paving and physically separate drainage/metal interfaces. Albedo, roughness, normal amplitude, wetness and physical UV scales are defined by the linked ground contracts.
domains.mounting: Horizontal finish zones bear on the ground support; kerbs, drain channels, covers and tree/root interfaces are seated into or against the paved/soil substrate instead of floating above it.
domains.interfacesGapsSeals: Paving-to-soil edges, kerb joints, drain slots, covers, root zones and contact margins must retain physical gaps/contact shadows at the scale specified by linked contracts.
domains.orientationExposure: Upward-facing exterior surfaces receive strong midsummer UV/rain; traffic routes receive wear and soil transfer; sheltered drain recesses retain more moisture and grime.
domains.aging: Cause-based foot traffic, splash, drainage and UV variation only; no arbitrary catastrophe damage, crater patterns or unexplained global dirt masks.
domains.geometryVsMaterial: Kerbs, joints, drains, level changes, roots/contact interfaces and silhouette-scale relief are geometry; aggregate, grains, pores, fine abrasion and wet/dry optical change are material response.
domains.lodPolicy: Silhouette/construction geometry uses explicit scene LOD policy where generated detail requires it; metre-scaled microdetail relies on mipmapped/aniso textures and must not create visible LOD pop.

domains.manufacture: RC apartment block with coated exterior concrete, balcony slabs, sliding aluminum sash, rail assemblies, service equipment, rainwater hardware, period-plausible rooftop receiving equipment and ordinary household textile occupancy assembled as physically distinct components.
domains.dimensionsThickness: Five-storey generated fallback uses approximately 2.55 m floor pitch and 4.15 m bay pitch; window, rail, fastener, AC, rainwater, rooftop and balcony-futon thickness/contact dimensions are specified in linked construction contracts.
domains.materialsFinish: Painted RC, dielectric glazing/seals/plastics/PVC, anodized aluminum, galvanized or stainless/exposed steel, interior curtain cloth and dry balcony bedding remain physically separated with material-specific PBR response.
domains.mounting: Sash and service hardware are fixed to openings/slabs; rails use base plates/fasteners; AC and pipes use brackets/collars/clamps; rooftop antenna uses ballast/support rails/mast hardware; balcony bedding uses a gravity-balanced physical drape around the actual top rail rather than a rigid slab floating in front of it.
domains.interfacesGapsSeals: Window perimeter seals, sash tracks, sill drips, balcony slab edges, rail bases, pipe penetrations, service collars, curtain-to-glass/backing depth, roof ballast contact and bedding-to-rail/slab clearances must be explicit and non-interpenetrating.
domains.orientationExposure: Facade, balcony and rooftop faces receive coherent midsummer sun/rain according to orientation; recesses and tracks retain more grime while upward sills/slabs receive water spotting and dust. Dry balcony bedding receives exterior UV but no current wet sheen.
domains.aging: UV chalking/fading, ledge runoff, ground splash, drain runoff, localized ferrous-source rust, service contact and ordinary textile wash/fold variation only; no arbitrary structural damage narrative.
domains.geometryVsMaterial: Openings, slab lips, extrusions, rails, seals, tracks, fasteners, brackets, cables, curtain pleats and centimetre-scale bedding loft/drape are geometry at observable scale; coating grain, oxidation, textile weave, fine scratches and residue optics are material/microdetail.
domains.lodPolicy: High-detail facade, curtain, rooftop, service and balcony textile assemblies use explicit LOD0/1/2/3 or documented construction-safe simplification with animated cross-fade where applicable; rendered pop remains a temporal critical check.

domains.manufacture: Ordinary neighborhood-park slide and bench fallback assembled from coated steel tube/plate, stainless slide surface, timber seating and precast/concrete supports using visible joins and supports.
domains.dimensionsThickness: Slide shell, access stair/stringer/bracket/guard/support interfaces and bench seat/support dimensions are recorded in the park/street-furniture and assembly-interface contracts; the slide running surface retains millimetre-scale physical thickness rather than a painted plane.
domains.materialsFinish: Aged coated steel, stainless/exposed metal, timber and precast concrete use separate PBR families with manufacture-scale texture structure, plausible metallic values and no baked highlights.
domains.mounting: Slide access stringers terminate on grade plates, each tread bears through welded side brackets, access rails join the platform guard, chute head/runout use explicit load paths, and bench supports meet ground while timber seating is supported/fastened rather than floating.
domains.interfacesGapsSeals: Ground contacts, tread/bracket/stringer joins, stair/platform transition, frame/chute bearings, fastener locations and timber/support interfaces must retain plausible clearances, intended overlap and contact shadow.
domains.orientationExposure: Outdoor equipment receives strong UV/rain; hand/foot contact, water runoff and near-ground splash vary wear by use and exposure.
domains.aging: Paint chalking, contact polish, stainless abrasion direction, timber UV/checking and ground splash follow causal exposure; no random damage layer.
domains.geometryVsMaterial: Tube/plate/shell thickness, stair treads, brackets, stringers, rails, load-bearing joins, supports and fastening are geometry; orange-peel, fine slide scratches, wood grain/checking and concrete pores are microtexture/material response.
domains.lodPolicy: LOD0 preserves physical construction and fine silhouette; LOD1/2/3 progressively reduce sub-pixel detail with cross-fade while retaining stair/support/bench load-path silhouettes that would otherwise create visible topology pops.

domains.manufacture: Planted landscape trees are modeled as biological root/trunk/branch/twig/leaf hierarchies with root-zone/soil interfaces and cause-based understory density rather than stacked primitive crowns.
domains.dimensionsThickness: Generated mature-tree height and branching/leaf scales vary by deterministic individual; root-zone, trunk, twig, leaf and understory dimensions are constrained by the vegetation ecology contract.
domains.materialsFinish: Bark is rough dielectric organic material; thin leaves use two-sided transmission optics; root-zone soil/precast interfaces remain non-metallic with exposure-dependent moisture response.
domains.mounting: Trunks emerge from root/soil interfaces; branches attach through hierarchy; leaves attach to twig/branch structure; understory originates from plausible soil/edge zones rather than floating cards.
domains.interfacesGapsSeals: Root flare/soil contact and tree-pit/paving interfaces require grounding/contact shadow; vegetation must not visibly interpenetrate hardscape hero geometry.
domains.orientationExposure: Canopy receives directional midsummer sun and sky fill; lower/recessed foliage is shaded/humid; foot-traffic pressure reduces understory near pedestrian routes.
domains.aging: Ordinary seasonal/maintenance variation only: UV, moisture, shade and pedestrian pressure. No storm damage or reconstruction cues.
domains.geometryVsMaterial: Root/trunk/branch/twig/leaf silhouette and grounding are geometry; bark microfissure, leaf venation/transmission and soil grains are material response.
domains.lodPolicy: Tree and understory renderers use explicit LOD levels/cross-fade; clone-risk QA rejects identical natural hierarchies; shimmer/LOD pop is judged only from sealed temporal evidence.

domains.manufacture: Neighborhood lamp and notice-board fallback assembled from concrete/steel support, luminaire diffuser/housing and a framed weatherproof notice-board case with recessed backing, passive printed notices, clear acrylic cover, EPDM retention, hinge/latch hardware and runoff hood appropriate to an ordinary circa-2000 public-space context.
domains.dimensionsThickness: Pole and diffuser dimensions are recorded by the park/street-furniture contract; the notice-board contract separately fixes 75 mm case depth, 18 mm backing, 3 mm clear cover, 10 mm gasket face, hinge/latch hardware and 0.4 mm paper thickness.
domains.materialsFinish: Concrete, coated/exposed metal, frosted dielectric lamp diffuser, rough backing/paper, matte EPDM and transparent dielectric acrylic remain separate material families with restrained roughness/metallicity and physical angular response.
domains.mounting: Pole and posts meet ground support; luminaire head attaches to the pole; the notice-board frame spans two posts, backing is recessed, papers seat on the backing, the clear cover is hinged/latching on the frame, and the drip hood bears on the top rail.
domains.interfacesGapsSeals: Pole-to-ground, head-to-pole and diffuser-housing joints remain plausible; notice-board papers contact backing within 1 mm, retain dry-air separation from the cover, cover edges seat inside the frame with EPDM retention, and hinge/latch axes remain on the corresponding rails.
domains.orientationExposure: Outdoor faces receive UV/rain; lamp and board upper surfaces collect dust/water; notice-board cover receives runoff/wiping while backing/papers stay sheltered; near-ground splash varies locally.
domains.aging: Ordinary weathering from UV, rain, dust, wiping and contact; papers fade/yellow independently behind the cover; no damage-story overlays.
domains.geometryVsMaterial: Pole/head/frame/case/backing/cover/gasket/hinges/latch/paper thickness and physical joints are geometry; concrete pores, paint orange-peel, diffuser frost, printed ink, paper fibre, acrylic wiping haze and fine board texture are material response.
domains.lodPolicy: Street-furniture LOD0 preserves physical silhouette/construction; the notice-board cover/case and five-notice occupancy persist through LOD1/2/3 while only sub-pixel pin heads are omitted, avoiding content-class or cover silhouette pop.

domains.manufacture: Container for authored-or-generated replacement assets. Each rendered slot inherits the manufacture/installation specification of the scene domain it replaces; this scope exists so replacement content cannot bypass metadata coverage by being parented outside the original fallback root.
domains.dimensionsThickness: Replacement assets must preserve the slot's physical envelope, construction thickness and interfaces unless their linked slot-specific contract explicitly supersedes the generated fallback.
domains.materialsFinish: Replacement assets must retain physically plausible material families and PBR values from their linked domain contracts; authored art does not exempt metallic/specular or baked-highlight rules.
domains.mounting: Slot anchors preserve world installation and interface positions for ground, building and vegetation replacements.
domains.interfacesGapsSeals: Authored replacements must maintain ground contact, wall/opening interfaces, seals/gaps and non-interpenetration at slot boundaries.
domains.orientationExposure: Replacement content inherits the scene's solar, rain, UV, contact and moisture exposure metadata.
domains.aging: Replacement weathering remains cause-based and period-authentic; arbitrary damage/story cues are not accepted.
domains.geometryVsMaterial: Authored geometry owns observable construction/silhouette; materials own microstructure and angular response, never painted illumination.
domains.lodPolicy: Authored replacements must supply or inherit LOD0/1/2/3 behavior appropriate to benchmark footprint; temporal evidence remains mandatory for visible-pop clearance.
